tools.description: Retrieves messages from a specified Google Chat conversation (Space, direct message (DM) or group DM) in Markdown format. Allows filtering by thread, time range, and number of messages. Additionally, the next page of messages can be retrieved to allow for more context. Private messages (messages only visible to a single user) are filtered out.

conversationId.description: Required. The ID of the conversation. A conversation can either be a space, direct message (DM) or group DM/Chat. Format: spaces/{space}

endTime.description: Optional. ISO 8601 timestamp to filter messages. Only messages created before this time will be returned.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of messages to return. The service may return fewer than this value. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum value is 50. If you use a value more than 50, it's automatically changed to 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous list_messages call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page.

startTime.description: Optional. ISO 8601 timestamp to filter messages. Only messages created after this time will be returned.

threadId.description: Optional. The ID of a specific thread within the conversation. If provided, only messages from this thread will be returned. If omitted, messages from all threads in the conversation are considered. Format: spaces/{space}/threads/{thread}

tools.description:
Searches for Google Chat messages using keywords and filters returning them in Markdown format. Works across all spaces the user has access to, or can be scoped to a specific conversation.

Follow this guidance when deciding to use `search_messages` vs other search or read tools:

- Use `search_messages` when looking for specific message content, keywords, mentions, links, senders or unread messages potentially across multiple spaces or without a known conversation ID.
- Use `list_messages` when you know the specific space or thread ID and want to read messages sequentially in chronological order.
- Use `search_conversations` to find space metadata such as conversation IDs by space display name or participants (it searches metadata only, not message contents).

If `searchParameters` is provided without specific filters, recent messages across conversations accessible to the user are returned.

SearchParameters.description: Configures the parameters used for searching messages. If `searchParameters` is provided with no sub-fields set, recent messages across conversations accessible to the user are returned.

conversationId.description: Optional. Scopes the search to a specific conversation identifier, as returned from the search_conversations tool. Format: `spaces/{ID}`.

conversationIncludesUser.description: Optional. Filter for messages in DMs and group chats that include the specific user email or ID.

conversationTypes.description: Optional. Filter by the type of conversation.

x-google-enum-descriptions: A group chat between 3 or more people.
A direct message between two humans, or a human and a Chat app.

endTime.description: Optional. Filter for messages created before this time. Format: ISO 8601 timestamp.

hasAttachment.description: Optional. Filter for messages containing at least one attachment. Note: This field is under development and may not be supported in all environments yet.

hasLink.description: Optional. Filter for messages containing at least one URL.

isUnread.description: Optional. Filter for messages that have not been read by the calling user.

keywords.description: Optional. A set of keywords which are used to filter the results.

mentionsMe.description: Optional. Filter for messages that explicitly mention the calling user.

sender.description: Optional. Filter for messages from a specific user. Either the email or resource name of the sender can be used. User resource names are formatted as `users/{ID}`, where `{ID}` can be a person ID or their email address.

spaceDisplayNames.description: Optional. Filter by a list of space names; space display names are partially matched. Note: Only the top 5 matches are returned.

startTime.description: Optional. Filter for messages created after this time. Format: ISO 8601 timestamp.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of results to return (max up to 100). If unspecified, at most 25 are returned.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous `search_messages` call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page.

searchParameters.description: Required. The search parameters to use for the search.

tools.description:
Searches for Google Chat conversations to find conversation IDs. Named spaces are found by display name (`space_name_query`). Direct messages (DMs) and group chats are found only by participant email addresses (`participants`).

This tool searches conversation metadata, NOT message contents. To search within message history or find messages by keyword/sender/timestamp, use `search_messages`.

If only `participants` are provided, this tool finds 1:1 direct messages (if one participant is provided) or group chats (if multiple participants are provided) that include the specified participants and the calling user. Named spaces are not returned.

If only a `space_name_query` is provided, this tool searches ONLY named spaces where the query is a case-insensitive substring of the space's display name. DMs and group chats are never returned, so do NOT pass a person's name as `space_name_query` to find a DM with them; look up their email address and pass it in `participants` instead.

If both `participants` and `space_name_query` are provided, this tool finds DMs or group chats by participants and then filters them by display name.

If neither `participants` nor `space_name_query` are provided, this tool lists named spaces the calling user is a member of (DMs and group chats are not included).

By default, this tool only lists conversations the calling user is a member of.

Do not set `discoverable_spaces` or `pending_invites` (fields in development) unless explicitly instructed; they are mutually exclusive with each other and with `participants`, and `space_name_query` must be at most 1000 characters (if the server returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` stating they are not enabled yet, retry without them):
- `discoverable_spaces = true`: searches named spaces in the caller's organization that are discoverable to the caller and that the caller has neither joined nor been invited to (`page_size` up to 50). Provide `space_name_query` for directory search, or omit it to browse recently active discoverable spaces.
- `pending_invites = true`: lists named spaces and group chats where the caller has a pending invitation, newest invitation first (`page_size` up to 1000; spam invitations and 1:1 direct message requests are excluded). Provide `space_name_query` to filter invitations by case-insensitive display-name substring.
- When paginating `discoverable_spaces` or `pending_invites` with `page_token`, keep `space_name_query`, `discoverable_spaces`, and `pending_invites` identical to the call that returned `nextPageToken`.

Returns a list of conversation objects containing conversation IDs (format: `spaces/{space}`), display names, conversation types, and last active timestamps.

IMPORTANT: An empty `conversations` list does not mean there are no more results overall. If `nextPageToken` is present, more pages can be fetched. If you get an empty list but a `nextPageToken`, ask the user if you should continue the searching.

discoverableSpaces.description: Optional. Field in development. Do not use unless explicitly instructed. If true, searches named spaces in the caller's organization that are discoverable to the caller and that the caller has neither joined nor been invited to. `space_name_query` performs a directory search (or browses recently active discoverable spaces when empty). Returned conversations are spaces the caller has not joined; use `conversation_id` to open or join them. Mutually exclusive with `pending_invites` and `participants`.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of spaces to return. The service may return fewer than this value. If unspecified, at most 20 spaces will be returned. The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 will be coerced to 1000. When `discoverable_spaces` is set, values above 50 are coerced to 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. A page token, received from a previous `search_conversations` call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. When `discoverable_spaces` or `pending_invites` is set, keep `space_name_query`, `discoverable_spaces`, and `pending_invites` identical to the call that returned the token; those page tokens are bound to the search mode and query and are rejected in any other mode.

participants.description: Optional. List of email addresses of the participants to filter the conversations, excluding the caller. Use this to find direct messages (DMs) and group chats: a single participant returns the 1:1 DM with that person, and multiple participants return group chats containing all of them. Named spaces are not returned when this field is set.

pendingInvites.description: Optional. Field in development. Do not use unless explicitly instructed. If true, lists the caller's pending invitations to named spaces and group chats, newest invitation first. Spam invitations are excluded and 1:1 direct message requests are not included. `space_name_query` filters the invitations by display name (case-insensitive substring match). Returned conversations are ones the caller has a pending invitation to. Mutually exclusive with `discoverable_spaces` and `participants`.

spaceNameQuery.description: Optional. The text to search for within conversation display names (case-insensitive substring match). If `participants` is empty, only named spaces are searched and direct messages (DMs) and group chats are never returned, so searching for a person's name here won't find a DM with them. To find a DM or group chat, provide the members' email addresses in `participants` instead. If `participants` is set, this query further filters the matched DMs or group chats by display name.

annotations.title: Sends a Google Chat message to a conversation

tools.description:
Sends a Google Chat message to a conversation with Markdown formatting and optional citations.

This tool uses a conversation ID, an optional thread ID, a message text, optional inline citations, and optional footer cited sources as inputs.

Conversation IDs can be found using the `search_conversations` tool.

It returns the created message.

Citation.description: Citations are inline references that can provide users more detailed information about the inline reference. Corresponding inline citations should be present in the message text wrapped with the `chat-citation` tag with attribute `data-id="{id}"`.

citedSources.description: Required. One or more sources attached to this citation hovercard. A maximum of 50 cited sources are allowed in total across all inline citations and footer sources in a message.

id.description: Required. Unique identifier matching the `data-id` attribute in the `chat-citation` tag (e.g. wrapping cited text with `chat-citation` and attribute `data-id="ID"`) in `messageText`. Must consist only of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens (1-63 characters). Must be unique among all citations in the message.

CitedSource.description: A reference to a source of information.

footer.description: Optional. Additional attribution text displayed in the card footer (e.g. domain name "developers.google.com" or author/org name).

imageUrl.description: Optional. URL of an image preview thumbnail (must use an https:// URL).

snippet.description: Optional. A short excerpt or snippet directly from the source. Displayed in the hovercard or footer. Plain text only. Maximum length is 1,000 characters.

title.description: Required. Plaintext title of the source (e.g., "Google Workspace Developer Preview Program"). Markdown formatting is not supported in titles.

url.description: Required. The URL of the cited resource (must be a valid http:// or https:// URL, e.g., "https://developers.google.com/workspace/preview").

cards.description: Optional. Cards attached to the message. Maximum size is 32 KB per card. Each card is represented as a JSON struct following the Google Chat Card format (Google Workspace UIKit Card / Cards v2). To attach cards to a message, the Chat app must be a member of the space. Images in cards aren't supported. Card identification: * The top-level `name` string field in each card serves as its identifier. * If multiple cards are attached to a message, each card MUST specify a unique, non-empty `name`.

conversationId.description: Required. The ID of the conversation (e.g., 'spaces/AAAA...') to send the message to.

footerCitedSources.description: Optional. Top-level cited sources displayed as reference cards at the bottom (footer) of the message. A maximum of 50 cited sources are allowed in total across all inline citations and footer sources in a message.

inlineCitations.description: Optional. Inline citations referenced within `messageText` via `chat-citation` tags. A maximum of 20 inline citations are allowed per message. Unreferenced inline citations (those without a matching `chat-citation` tag in `messageText`) are ignored and do not cause a validation error.

messageText.description: Required. The main content of the message. Formatting can be added using standard Markdown (note that tables are NOT supported). The following formatting is supported: * **Bold:** `**text**` * **Italic:** `*text*` or `_text_` * **Strikethrough:** `~~text~~` * **Monospace:** `text` * **Monospace block:** ``` line 1 line 2 ``` * **Bulleted list:** * item 1 * item 2 * **Ordered list:** 1. item 1 2. item 2 * **Block quote:** `> quoted text` * **Hyperlink:** `[label](url)` * **Mention user:** Use a self-closing HTML tag `chat-user` with attributes `data-email="user@example.com"` or `data-user="users/USER_ID"`. Prefer the `data-user` attribute with `USER_ID` if known and fall back to the data-email attribute with the user email otherwise. If you use the `data-user` attribute make sure to include the users/ prefix seen in other tool return values. Note: A maximum of 10 mentions are allowed per message. Mentioning all users (e.g., using `@all` or an HTML tag with `users/all`) is strictly prohibited. * **Custom emoji:** Use a self-closing HTML tag `chat-emoji` with attributes `data-custom-emoji="customEmojis/abc"` or `data-emoji-name=":xyz:"`. * **Citation:** Wrap the cited text in an HTML tag `chat-citation` with the `data-id` attribute matching the citation ID. If a `chat-citation` tag has a `data-id` that does not match any `Citation.id`, the tag is ignored and the wrapped text is rendered as plain text. Note: A maximum of 20 inline citations are allowed per message.

threadId.description: Optional. The ID of the thread (e.g., 'spaces/AAAA.../threads/BBBB...') to send the message to. If not set, the message will be sent to a new thread.
